bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO — consensus PT upgrade wave, shares +24-29% pre-market
bullets.body: NVIDIA's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO, and board director with US government input (Trump called into the board meeting) confirming no national security risk. Analyst upgrades poured in: Citi raised PT to $240 (from $225, 15x FY28E EPS, Buy), Melius upgraded to Buy with $220 PT (33% upside), Bernstein upgraded to Outperform with $200 PT, while Wolfe Research maintained Outperform at $200 (59% upside). KeyBanc remains Sector Weight at $160, citing ongoing investigations (Chinese intelligence contact, Megaspeed export probes, delayed 10-Q, House committee interviews). New National Security and Export Control Committee formed; CCO search underway.

bullets.title: CRWD acquires ZS for ~$43.9B all-stock — $1B revenue synergy target, low antitrust risk
bullets.body: CrowdStrike announced an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler at 1.135x CRWD shares per ZS share (~$260/share, 34% premium), valuing the deal at ~$43.9B. Combined ARR exceeds $10B; CRWD targets ~$1B annualized revenue synergies by 30 months post-close and ~$500M cost synergies within 18-24 months. UBS sees low horizontal antitrust risk (CRWD=endpoint, ZS=network security); deal expected accretive to FCF immediately. CRWD also raised FY27 guidance with NNARR $1.459-1.463B (+44-45% y/y); Falcon Guardian (AI agent security) surpassed $100M ARR. UBS rates both CRWD and ZS Buy at $250 PT each.

bullets.title: DASH: Hedgeye adds to top short list — Instacart deal resets cycle, Amazon-Uber threat material
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Deep Dive argues DASH is a top short: the $17B Instacart acquisition resets the investment cycle and pushes earnings benefits into the future, while Uber's 55M Uber One members and zero-cost distribution via commerce app pose material share risk. Core restaurant business held on check not traffic; disinflation in 1H27 makes sustaining prices harder. DASH transitions from asset-light marketplace to fixed costs/logistics, and AI assistants (Google, POS vendors) are bypassing the marketplace entirely. Instacart order growth was flat all year; top 3 retailers represent 43% of GTV.

bullets.title: APP (AppLovin): US eCommerce store growth accelerates to record 3.4% weekly in 4Q26
bullets.body: Citi tracks AppLovin's eCommerce client base at 23,434 globally as of Nov 20, with US stores at 7,693 (+5.2% w/w, the largest weekly increase to date). US store growth accelerated from 1.5% average weekly in 3Q26 to 3.4% in 4Q26 QTD. Caveat: average store rank deteriorated to 435 from 397, suggesting lower-quality stores are adopting the platform. International stores (HK/China dropshippers) growing 7.2% w/w and represent 47.6% of total. Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: TTWO: GTA VI sets entertainment record at $3.79B day-one sales, 40.5M copies
bullets.body: Take-Two's GTA VI achieved $3.79B in day-one retail sales (32.5M pre-release + ~8M day-of units = ~40.5M total), the highest launch in entertainment history, well above prior expectations. B Riley raised estimates and maintained Buy at $300 PT. Mix skewed toward the $99.99 Ultimate edition. Primary remaining catalysts: 3-day sales figures, PC version, and eventual online version.

bullets.title: META: MS raises Opex estimates to $227B, cuts 2027/2028 EPS by 13%/11%; PT lowered to $720
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised META's Opex estimates to $227B on higher cloud/AI spend, cutting 2027 and 2028 EPS estimates by -13% and -11% respectively, with the price target lowered to $720. Separately, MS highlights Gemini 4 Hydrogen (GOOGL) showing ~4X efficiency improvements over prior gen as a key model multiplier to watch into 2027, with both GOOGL and META agentic rollout in focus.

bullets.title: AMZN: Acquires AI startup Decart for ~$7.5B to advance custom silicon and AI inference
bullets.body: Amazon confirmed an agreement to purchase Decart's proprietary Optimization Stack (DOS) technology with the co-founders and research team joining Amazon, aimed at optimizing AI inference and advancing custom silicon. FT reported the price at $7.5B; transaction subject to regulatory clearance. Separately, ClickHouse expanded its AWS partnership with a $1.5B investment commitment and 4x higher go-to-market funding.

bullets.title: DKNG: NFL Week 11 all-5 biggest favorites won — possible Q4 hold-rate headwind
bullets.body: UBS notes NFL Week 11 saw 9/12 favorites win with all 5 biggest moneyline spread favorites winning — a 75%+ favorite-win rate that has occurred only 4.6 weeks per season historically. DKNG expects normal sportsbook hold if 3-4 of 5 biggest favorites win; 5/5 wins imply lower hold, potentially a risk to Q4 guidance. UBS has already downgraded DKNG to Neutral. DKNG is also at a 52-week low, down 45.1% YTD at $15.90.

bullets.title: INTU: Sells Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for ~$3.68B — Intuit reinvests $368M in acquirer equity
bullets.body: Bending Spoons is acquiring Mailchimp from Intuit at ~$3.68B enterprise value (deal closing early 2027), with Intuit reinvesting $368M into Bending Spoons equity. JPM initiated Bending Spoons at Neutral/$48 PT. Separately, Klein's Quick Bytes notes INTU faces headwinds from Credit Karma but sees valuations attractive at 9x NTM FCF, 12x NTM P/E after the selloff.

bullets.title: CRM: Citi cuts PT to $198 from $263 on sluggish core growth, limited production AI deployments
bullets.body: Citi cut its CRM price target from $263 to $198, citing sluggish core growth and limited production AI deployments. This comes ahead of CRM's earnings preview. MDB remains a top Citi pick with expectations for ~29% Q3 Atlas growth and a raise to Q4 guidance.

bullets.title: MU: UBS semis call cuts data center estimates; MU at ~$325 (2x TBV) seen as 'AI trade is over' signal
bullets.body: UBS semiconductor analyst Tim Arcuri hosted a call cutting data center estimates across coverage, aligning with LPS guidance. UBS flagged MU at ~$325 (2x TBV) could represent the market pricing 'AI trade is over,' currently two-thirds of the way to that scenario. Semis NTM P/E are ~10-15% above 2018 and post-COVID trough levels, suggesting a potential tactical bottom is forming but memory pricing must stabilize first.

bullets.title: ACN: UBS initiates Buy at $300 PT — CRWD/ZS deal validates 15% cyber revenue opportunity
bullets.body: UBS initiated Accenture at Buy with a $300 PT (based on ~17x 2029E EPS), arguing the CRWD-ZS deal reinforces demand for cybersecurity services consolidation. Accenture's cyber business represents ~15% of revenue; historical analog is cloud, which grew from $0.8B (2011) to $37B (2024). Accenture has acquired 24 cyber companies since 2015.

bullets.title: TSLA: MS highlights FSD v15 rollout and $3K hardware cost advantage driving AV thesis
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes Tesla rolled out FSD v15 with photorealistic reality view (Musk calls it 'banger release' and 'super intelligence'). MS also highlights Tesla's Full Self-Driving hardware costs ~$3K vs Waymo Level 4 at ~$30K, positioning TSLA for rapid AV adoption with China expected to capture disproportionate early share.

bullets.title: RBLX: Week 47 CCUs down 17% YoY — GTA VI had negligible impact, 4Q26 bookings tracking $1.92B
bullets.body: Citi tracks Roblox Week 47 average peak CCUs at 14.5M, down 17% YoY but only -1% sequentially vs. prior week, suggesting GTA VI's Nov 19 release had negligible impact. 4Q26 bookings tracking $1.92B, below the mid-point of guidance ($1.89B-$2.0B) and below Visible Alpha consensus of $1.97B.

bullets.title: DIS: Raises cash dividend 33% to $2.00/share; COHR authorizes $2B buyback
bullets.body: Disney raised its cash dividend by 33% to $2.00 per share, while Coherent authorized a $2B share repurchase program, per StreetAccount's weekly dividend/buyback summary (week of Nov 16-22).

bullets.title: SHOP/CLS: Canadian tech names surge 9%+ amid broad TSX rally (+3.1%)
bullets.body: Shopify (SHOP.CN) surged +9.6% and Celestica (CLS.CN) +9.1% as the TSX Composite climbed 3.1% to 34,218, led by precious metals and crypto mining names. The rally was driven by the AI rebound following Jensen Huang's reinstatement.

bullets.title: SNOW/PLTR: Upcoming analyst events signal continued institutional focus
bullets.body: JPM is hosting a Snowflake deep-dive webinar (Nov 24) with Accenture's Elite-Tier SNOW partner to discuss customer adoption, data migration, and competitive landscape. Goldman Sachs is hosting a PLTR product demo recap call (Nov 24) with analyst Gabriela Borges to discuss enterprise software positioning vs. MSFT.

bullets.title: BE/SEI: MS names top picks in distributed power as data center backlash drives BYOP adoption
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley identifies Bloom Energy (BE) and SEI as top picks in distributed power, arguing data center backlash from midterms elevates bring-your-own-power adoption. SOFCs rank #1 in MS's composite scorecard (4.5/5) on emissions and noise/footprint. MS estimates ~185 GW gross US data center power demand through 2029 with ~74 GW shortfall, and sees selective buying opportunities in BE, SEI, LBRT, BKR, FTAI after recent pullback.

bullets.title: DELL/STX/WDC: MS sees server valuations near historical troughs but flags -30% earnings haircut risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes Asia investors are debating CY2027 cloud capex cuts (not just moderation), with DELL/STX/WDC server valuations near historical troughs. A -30% earnings haircut on servers yields DELL $180 (downside -35%) and HPE $31 (downside -24%). DELL also surged 22.5% on unusual volume ahead of earnings after close.

bullets.title: TXN: Cantor Fitzgerald upgrades to Overweight, raises PT to $385 from $340
bullets.body: Texas Instruments was upgraded to Overweight from Neutral by Cantor Fitzgerald with a price target raised to $385 from $340, per pre-market tech sector summary.
